paragraphs.text: Apple plans to unveil its first smart glasses at its WWDC developer conference in June 2027 and begin shipping them before the end of 2027, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported in his Power On newsletter on November 15, 2026, according to MacRumors and Tbreak.

The first model will not include an augmented reality display. Wearers interact with the glasses through Siri, which uses built-in cameras to answer questions about their surroundings. Planned uses include identifying buildings, giving directions, translating signs and conversations, and suggesting meals based on what is in a refrigerator.
The iPhone does the heavy lifting

Software runs on a paired iPhone, which handles the processing and memory limits of the glasses. Developers will not need to build separate glasses apps. Instead they will let Siri control specific features of their existing iPhone apps. Gurman's examples include booking restaurant tables, requesting rides, ordering coffee, shopping and buying movie tickets.

Only recent iPhone models will be supported, and there will be no Android support. The glasses include Wi-Fi so some functions keep working when the phone is not nearby, but they will not be fully standalone. Built-in functions are expected to cover calls, messages, notifications, calendars, reminders, music and smart home controls.

MacRumors reported that Apple began adding the needed Siri app control features in the first iOS 27.3 beta, released in November. Support for Apple's own apps is planned for December, with third party support in 2027.
Hardware and the race with Meta

The prototypes, code-named N50, are reportedly slightly thinner than Meta's second generation Ray-Ban glasses. Some test units have oval camera openings built flush into the frame, and a front light shows when the glasses are in use or charging. They reportedly run a reduced version of visionOS on a processor derived from older Apple Watch chips, and Apple is stressing audio quality for music, calls and FaceTime.

Prototypes can charge while being worn, using a small flat magnetic connector near the left temple arm that MacRumors said is roughly the size of a Tic Tac. Apple is reportedly developing several styles and colors, and work on the glasses began in the early 2020s.

Apple sees its App Store ecosystem as a main advantage over Meta, the current market leader. Gurman also said the software and AI work is running late, which could delay the 2027 launch. Price, battery life and the final product name have not been reported, and Apple has not confirmed the plans.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the design puts Siri at the center of Apple's next hardware category. Without a display, the glasses are only as useful as the assistant's ability to understand a scene and act inside other apps, an area where Apple has been behind rivals.
Watch how Siri app control performs in the iOS 27.3 betas and in December's rollout to Apple's own apps, since the glasses depend on it.
